cues.text: Each row of the Orders sheet is one sale. Add up the Revenue column month by month, and you get these three bars.
Sales fall every month: about 117 thousand, then 106, then 101.
The Targets sheet asks for more each month. Here's the total of the four regions' targets.
July beats its target. August and September fall short, and the gap gets wider.
Across the whole quarter, sales come to 324 thousand against a target of 353, about 8 percent short.
August isn't a slow month. It sold more units than any other month: 849.
But every grinder and espresso machine went out at 15 to 25 percent off, all month long.
At full price, August would have reached 125 thousand, above its target. The discount pulled it under, and profit fell from 49 thousand in July to 34 thousand.
September has a different cause. Split the sales by region.
Three regions hold roughly level. North even has its best month.
West drops from 30 thousand in July to 13 thousand in September, less than half.
Most of that is West's retail orders. They fell from 58 in July to 16. The sheet shows it happened, but not why.
